Phoropter indexes with scip-typescript and nothing else, so a symbol anchor in any other language doesn't resolve. The first repository that wants one is this one: the TUI is Go, and every plan written for it has used file anchors instead. Batik kept indexes per indexer, made a missing one a no-index view, and loads an indexer only when something needs indexing. This plan makes indexers pluggable.

It's the plugin plan's first half. Indexers and UIs are different contracts: an indexer is a step in the build, chosen by the scheme an anchor names. A UI is a reader of the pages, chosen by the person. UIs come next.

Jeff's test for it: he has code that indexes .NET with Roslyn, and he'd like to hand it and this plan's guide to an agent and see what happens. So the contract can't assume SCIP, and the guide has to stand on its own. An agent writing an indexer should never need to open src/.

Decision: An indexer is a program that prints definitions as JSON

where (new) indexers/README.md file page

made by the work, so there is nothing to resolve

Because (Jeff, then Claude): "having a directory here with the go, typescript, whatever." A program in any language can satisfy one plain contract:

  • In: a directory holding the repository checked out at one commit, and the names of the packages the anchors ask for.
  • Out, on stdout: one JSON object, in the store's shape. It names the indexer, its version, the scheme it serves, and for each package it found, every definition: the symbol (version written as .), file, first line, last line.
  • Packages it can't find are listed as missing. A failure is a non-zero exit with one line on stderr. Phoropter turns either into no-index views, never a failed build.

SCIP indexers are adapters: they run the SCIP tool and turn its .scip into this JSON. Roslyn, or anything else that knows where definitions are, can print it directly.

Decision: The scheme an anchor names picks its indexer

where src/scip.ts file page

quote export function isScipSymbol(where: string): boolean {

Because (Claude, not asked): a symbol anchor already starts with its scheme (scip-typescript npm …, scip-go gomod …). Symbols keep SCIP's grammar, scheme, manager, package, version, descriptors, for every indexer, so anchors read alike in any language. A scheme needn't start with scip-, so a Roslyn indexer can name its own (roslyn nuget …). Phoropter groups the packages each document's anchors ask for by scheme and runs each scheme's indexer once per commit for its packages.

Decision: First-party indexers live in indexers/, others are found on PATH

where src/site.ts file page

quote export function packagesOf(cx: Context, docs: Doc[]): Set<string> {

Because (Jeff, then Claude): indexers/<name>/ holds each first-party indexer, with an indexer.json naming its scheme and the command that runs it. Any other indexer is a program on PATH named phoropter-index-<scheme>, the way gh finds extensions, so there's nothing to configure. Phoropter looks in indexers/ first, then on PATH. Your .NET indexer could live either way: in indexers/dotnet/ if it joins this repository, or installed on its own. "Good enough for gh and kubectl, good enough for us" (Jeff), and indexers/README.md documents it. A config file in the repository was weighed.

Decision: scip-typescript moves into indexers/typescript/

where src/scip.ts file page

quote function scipTypescript(): { scip: any; main: string } {

Because (Claude, not asked): the first indexer shows the contract, and it shouldn't be special. What src/scip.ts does today (find the package roots by package.json name, run scip-typescript, keep the definitions) becomes indexers/typescript/, a program that prints the JSON. src/ keeps only what every indexer shares: running one, reading its output, and the symbol grammar. Mock-control's pages come out the same before and after, which the tests check.

Decision: A Go indexer in indexers/go/, so this repository's plans can anchor symbols

where tui/go.mod file page

quote module phoropter-tui

Because (Claude, not asked): a contract with one implementation isn't tested yet, and the TUI is the case that's been waiting. indexers/go/ finds a package root by its go.mod module path (here, phoropter-tui in tui/) and prints its definitions. The TUI's next plan can anchor scip-go gomod phoropter-tui . internal/tui/… and phoropter shows it at the base, the as-built head, and now. It wraps scip-go: it runs it and turns the .scip into the JSON. Its symbols are the ones Go's SCIP users already know, Sourcegraph maintains it, and it's the fastest and cheapest way there (Jeff: "whatever you think is fastest, cheapest"). It takes one go install on a machine that indexes Go. Where it isn't installed, Go anchors show no-index. Its own program on go/packages was weighed.

Decision: The guide for writing an indexer is indexers/README.md

where guide.md file page

quote Or a SCIP symbol, with the package version written as `.` so a release doesn't

Because (Jeff): "a 'how to create an indexer' guide." It's written for an agent handed only the guide and an existing piece of code: the contract, the symbol grammar with examples in three languages, the JSON shape with a complete example, how package roots are usually found, what to do about versions, and how to check the result. The plan guide's section on symbol anchors links it, and says how to find a symbol's string.

Decision: phoropter index --check tests an indexer against the contract

where (new) src/check.ts file page

made by the work, so there is nothing to resolve

Because (Claude, not asked): "see how it goes" needs a way to tell. phoropter index --check <program> [path] runs an indexer on a repository at HEAD and checks its output: the JSON's shape, that every file exists at that commit, that every range is inside its file, and that each definition's name appears in its range. It prints what failed and why. An agent writing an indexer runs it until it passes, and so can a reviewer.

Decision: phoropter symbols <file> lists the symbols defined in a file

where (new) src/cli.ts file page

made by the work, so there is nothing to resolve

Because (Claude, not asked): nobody types scip-go gomod phoropter-tui . internal/tui/docScreen#annotate(). from memory, an agent included. phoropter symbols tui/internal/tui/screens.go prints each symbol defined there with its lines, from the store, indexing if it must, and ready to paste into a plan's where:. It's how anchors get written in a language the writer hasn't anchored in before.

Decline: A .NET indexer, in this plan

Because (Jeff): that's the test of the guide, not part of the work. An agent given Jeff's Roslyn code and indexers/README.md writes it, after this lands.

Decline: Changing the store's layout for schemes

Because (Claude, not asked): batik keys a stored index by commit and package. Two schemes could name the same package, but each stored file already names its indexer and scheme, so a mismatch reads as missing and is indexed again rather than misread. Adding the scheme to the path would revisit batik for a collision nobody has had.

Guess: An agent with only indexers/README.md and existing code writes an indexer that passes --check

Answered in the as-built: not tested.

Disproved if: given Jeff's Roslyn code and the guide, the agent has to read src/, asks something the guide should have answered, or ends with an indexer that phoropter index --check fails on a .NET repository.
